The printed MTB coefficient is 0.0000 in Table 3 column (1) while its t-statistic is 4.028; the coefficient is preserved at its printed precision and is not treated as an exact zero.

Source-first scope: the introduction explicitly frames the information-environment analysis around two main outcomes, the adverse-selection component of the spread (GHLAMBDA) and ERCs. Retain the full eight-quarter comment-letter-firm specification for each: Table 3 Panel B column (1) and Table 4 column (2). The source calls the propensity-score matched comparison a robustness check and the one-quarter window a causality-confidence analysis; these, the Table 4 reduced SUE-only column, amendment/content analyses, and voluntary-disclosure alternative explanation are excluded.

The two retained outcome regressions use the authors’ described pre/post Equation (1) design; the paper does not identify the underlying estimator. Firm/year fixed effects and firm-clustered heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors are reported.

Supporting fits are retained for the actually estimated GHLAMBDA stock-month construction and the fitted controls PERSIST, PREDICT, and BETA. Equation (2) uses the supplied coordinator-verified mathematical transcription. The persistence fit is described in prose; the BETA fit is identified as a market model but its equation and underlying estimator are not reported.
results_review_notes: The selected baseline results are Table 3 Panel B column (1), the comment-letter-firm eight-quarter information-asymmetry model, and Table 4 column (2), the comment-letter-firm full ERC model. Matched-sample, one-quarter, baseline-only, and appendix models are excluded.

Table 3 Panel A provides pre/post descriptives for every retained GHLAMBDA outcome and predictor. The ERC model has no directly relevant descriptive-statistics table located; Appendix A1 descriptives concern the separate propensity-score determinant models and are not linked to this baseline.

Table 3 reports firm and year fixed effects as included, but does not tabulate individual fixed-effect coefficients. Table 4 column (2) also omits a standalone intercept; the source does not say whether a constant is absorbed by fixed effects.

Both result tables identify t-statistics, firm-clustered robust standard errors, and two-tailed marker thresholds. Formal test-family labels and degrees of freedom are not reported; exact p-values are not inferred from markers.

GHLAMBDA is described as the quarterly average of lambda after multiplying retained monthly lambda estimates by 1,000 for presentation; all table estimates and descriptives are preserved on the source-reported scale.

Table 3 Panel A provides the complete descriptive rows for GHLAMBDA and its six information-asymmetry controls in pre/post quarters. Table A1 Panel A and Panel D also summarize retained SIZE in distinct firm-year matching samples; those four SIZE rows are kept in separate groups with the source-stated timing and different-sample relation. No source descriptive rows were found for CAR, SUE, POST, or the other ERC-only baseline terms.
